name: PT Supreme Cable Manufacturing & Commerce Tbk
industry_name: Industrial goods, building products & electrical equipment

frontmatter.title: Supreme Cable: a net-cash cable maker inside the grid build-out
frontmatter.summary: We initiate with BUY and Rp5,504, 113.3% above the price (a 120.4% total return with the Rp182 dividend). The market pays 3.8x forward earnings for a debt-free cable maker holding IDR1,223.5bn of cash, with 43,308 t of installed copper capacity and a grid pipeline behind it; what the price lacks is not earnings but a reason to believe the cash belongs to minorities.
thesis: The balance sheet is the thesis: IDR1,223.5bn of cash and no borrowings mean a large share of the IDR2,121.6bn market capitalisation is cash, and the operating business is bought on 1.1x EV/EBITDA.
Copper is passed through rather than absorbed: FY2025 gross margin of 8.7% widened to 10.3% in our FY2026E as inventory bought below spot is sold at spot [S0][S2].

Volume is the FY2027 story, not the FY2026 one: nine-month revenue grew far more slowly than the copper price, so our FY2026E revenue implies copper consumption below 25,160 t against 43,308 t of capacity; the 702 IDR trn of PLN projects is the pool that refills it [S0][S2][S7].
Reported book value misleads in both directions: 2,760 IDR bn of equity is a PSAK 16 revaluation surplus, so the shares trade at a discount to pre-revaluation book, not the reported multiple [S2].

The register is the risk, but not through float: the public holds 24.9%, above the exchange minimum; two family vehicles hold 33.6% and 29.7%, 78.7% of revenue is sold to related-party distributors and 86.9% of purchases come from the related rod supplier, which is why a 120.4% return can persist without closing [S2].

catalysts.event: PLN tender programme for grid projects awarded; cable orders follow into 2027
FY2026 audited results: does the nine-month gross-margin gain survive the Q4 copper mark-to-market?

H1 2027 accounts: first full half against the copper deck normalisation

blocks.text: We initiate on PT Supreme Cable Manufacturing & Commerce Tbk (SUCACO) with a **BUY** rating and a twelve-month target of **Rp5,504**, which is 113.3% above the Rp2,580 price - a 120.4% total return once the Rp182 dividend is added. The target is the weighted, liquidity-discounted value across our three methods; the base case alone is worth Rp6,226 and the undiscounted weighted value Rp6,880.

The variant view is uncomfortable rather than clever: at Rp2,580 the market is valuing the operating business at almost nothing once the cash and the associate are taken out. The market capitalisation is IDR2,121.6bn against IDR1,223.5bn of cash at the last audited year-end and an associate stake worth a further fraction of the price, so the enterprise is being asked to carry a cable plant, a national distributor network and 43,308 t of capacity for a low single-digit multiple of EBITDA. We do not claim a governance discount is wrong to exist - a family-controlled company that buys the great majority of its rod from an associate and sells 78.7% of its output to related distributors deserves one - only that the discount implied by the price is several times the one we apply, and the section below decomposes it rather than asserting it.

Why the discount exists is not mysterious: two family vehicles hold 33.6% and 29.7% of the shares, the controlling shareholder is also President Commissioner, 78.7% of revenue is sold to related-party distributors, 86.9% of purchases come from a related rod supplier, and IDR354.6m of daily traded value cannot absorb an institutional position [S2]. The public float is 24.9%, so this is not a float-compliance discount - the data pack's 9.1% is a registry classification that understates the audited shareholder register - it is a control and marketability discount. We apply a 20.0% liquidity discount for exactly that reason, and we do not pretend it will close on our timetable. What we will not do is pretend the earnings are not real: the company has paid a cash dividend every year in our sample, funded capex and dividends from operating cash flow without borrowing, and carries an unmodified audit opinion [S2].

Three things move the value. First the copper pass-through. Copper averaged US$9,939/t in FY2025 and LME three-month metal stood at US$13,880/t in November 2026 [S2][S6]; cable prices follow the metal, so revenue rises mechanically while the conversion margin - the part the company keeps - is set by competitive tension and inventory timing. Our FY2026E gross margin of 10.3% is not a forecast of pricing power; it is what the company printed in the third quarter, held into the fourth [S0]. Second, volume: copper consumed was 25,160 t against 43,308 t of capacity in FY2025, but the nine-month revenue tells us FY2026 tonnage is running below that, so utilisation is a FY2027 recovery story tied to the 702 IDR trn tender programme and the 3,290 IDR trn ten-year investment plan [S0][S2][S7]. Third, capital allocation: with no debt and a payout of about a quarter of earnings, the cash builds unless it is returned or deployed, and either outcome is worth more than the current price - provided it is not diverted.

The honest counter-case is in the risk section and it is not small. A converter's revenue is a copper price with a margin attached; if the metal falls faster than inventory is marked, the margin compresses and a cheap multiple on peak-copper earnings becomes an ordinary multiple on trough earnings. Our bear case is still worth Rp4,531, which is the point: the downside is protected by cash and book value, not by growth.

Cable manufacturing is a conversion business. The producer buys copper rod and aluminium, draws and strands it, applies insulation and sheathing, and sells by the metre to distributors, utilities and contractors. Because the metal dominates unit cost, revenue tracks the copper price while gross profit tracks the spread between rod input and the quoted cable price, plus whatever inventory gain or loss the pricing lag creates. The economics resemble a tolling operation with working-capital risk; the competitive variables are scale, certification and distribution rather than product differentiation.

SUCACO is one of Indonesia's established power-cable manufacturers. The company was founded in 1970, listed in 1982 as the first domestic-investment (PMDN) issuer on the exchange, and describes itself as a market leader in the cable industry [S2]. It employs 837 people from a Jakarta head office and manufacturing base [S0].

**What it makes.** The range spans the voltage ladder: high-voltage, medium-voltage armoured and non-armoured, lead-sheath and spacer cable, low-voltage power cable, building wire, flexible and instrument cable, solar cable, fire-resistant and airport-lighting cable, OPGW and fibre optic, telecommunication and LAN cable, bare conductor and ACCC, enamelled wire and railway cable [S0]. The breadth is commercially relevant - it lets the company bid a project package rather than a single specification and keeps the distributor relationship wide.

**How it is organised.** Two reported segments: cable, with FY2025 revenue of 7,200 IDR bn, and insulation and melamine, at 184 IDR bn [S2]. The group also consolidates a pelletising subsidiary, PT Setia Pratama Lestari Pelletizing Industries, whose minority contribution is immaterial, and liquidated PT Supreme Decoluxe in November 2025 with no material effect on the consolidated accounts [S2].

**Where the revenue comes from.** Power cable dominates cable sales, with telecommunication cable and enamelled wire small contributors [S2]. By market, 79.9% of FY2025 cable sales went to the private sector, overwhelmingly through the distributor network the annual report calls the backbone of its marketing, with PLN and project work making up the balance [S2]. The qualification the distribution narrative can hide is that the channel is largely internal to the group: related parties bought 5,838 IDR bn of the company's output in FY2025, 78.7% of revenue, of which the largest single customer, PT Sibalec, took 25.2% and the four related distributors above ten per cent each took 70.0% [S2]. So "private sector" is not a diversified end-market: it is a small number of affiliated trading companies. This is a distribution business wearing a manufacturing coat - private-sector sales are small lots through resellers rather than single large tenders, which smooths revenue but hands pricing power to the channel, and the channel's economics are negotiated between affiliates.

**Strategy.** Management's stated priorities are better procurement of primary raw materials, operational efficiency, participation in every PLN tender across rural electrification, distribution, transmission and generation, close cooperation with the contractors that procure for PLN, and product development aimed at specific projects including oil and gas and large manufacturing plants [S2]. The FY2026 plan, set before the copper spike, targeted cable-segment sales and net profit of 300 IDR bn [S2]; nine months into the year profit has already exceeded that target, which says more about the plan's conservatism than about demand [S0].

**Ownership and group.** The company is family-controlled. The annual report's register at 31 December 2025 is explicit: PT Moda Sukma holds 33.6%, PT Tutulan Sukma 29.7%, Furukawa Electric Co., Ltd. of Japan 11.8%, and the public below five per cent each 24.9% [S2]. Elly Soepono is disclosed as indirect controlling shareholder and serves as President Commissioner; Surya Adiwijaya Soepono sits on the board as Commissioner [S2]. Furukawa is a strategic rather than a family holder - it has supplied technical assistance since the company began production in 1972 - and it accounts for most of the gap between the audited register and the data pack's 75.8% insider and 9.1% float split, which is a different registry classification [S2][S0]. There are about 822.3 million shares in issue after the share split of March 2024 [S2].

**Competitive position.** SUCACO is an incumbent, not a challenger, but the industry is fragmented and the annual report is candid that 2025 brought more intense competition on pricing, payment schemes and delivery times, new entrants, and copper and aluminium volatility [S2]. We treat it as one of a handful of credible full-range suppliers rather than a price-setter.

**Demand: the grid is the customer.** Indonesian cable demand is a derivative of electricity capex. PLN plans to tender 702 IDR trn of strategic projects by the end of 2026 - generation, transmission and substations - explicitly outside its ten-year business plan [S7]. The 2025-2034 RUPTL itself requires 3,290 IDR trn of investment over the decade, including roughly ten thousand circuit-kilometres of transmission [S7]. On top of that, PLN estimates that data-centre and AI load could require new generation capacity approaching 90.0 GW [S3]. Every one of those projects consumes cable: transmission conductor and OPGW, medium-voltage distribution cable, low-voltage service cable and building wire. This is the most important external variable for the company, and it is a policy variable rather than a market one.

**Supply: copper is tight and expensive.** LME three-month copper stood at US$13,880/t in November 2026 against the US$9,939/t average the company paid in FY2025 [S6][S2]. The tightness is structural: Indonesian mine supply is constrained while Grasberg ramps, concentrate and scrap are scarce, and exchange inventories have drawn down [S6]. For a converter this is a cost and working-capital problem more than a demand problem - the metal has to be financed, and price reversals hit inventory. The forecast, as opposed to the spot print, comes from the house metals driver registry (fund record), which carries copper at US$13,692/t for FY2026E and US$11,000/t from FY2027E on the World Bank Commodity Markets Outlook of April of April 2026, 2027 forecast - a mean-reversion anchor reviewed by the basic-materials sector lead on 27 October 2026, not a spot-price extrapolation.

**Regulation.** Three strands matter. Tender-based procurement by PLN sets payment terms and price competition. Local-content (TKDN) rules favour domestic manufacturers over imports and are a genuine barrier to entry. And the copper input is largely imported or bought from domestic rod makers, so rupiah weakness raises the working-capital requirement. We could not source an authoritative published size for the Indonesian cable market; the honest statement is that demand is visible through PLN's pipeline, not through an industry statistical series we can cite [S7][S2].

**Five forces.** Buyer power is high: related-party distributors are the channel for most of sales and PLN runs tenders for most of the rest [S2]. Supplier power is concentrated to the point of being a governance issue - one related party, PT Tembaga Mulia Semanan, supplied 86.9% of all purchases in FY2025 [S2]. The threat of entry is real at the low-voltage end, which is why the annual report flags new competitors, but certification, TKDN and the capital cost of a drawing and insulation line deter entry at medium and high voltage. Substitution is limited because copper is the conductor, though aluminium substitution exists in some distribution applications and is visible in the company's own falling aluminium consumption [S2]. Rivalry is the dominant force: the product is specified, not branded, and the annual report leads its constraints with competition [S2].

**Moat assessment.** We would not call this a wide moat. The defensible assets are a distributor network reaching private-sector buyers in small lots, a range and certification set that make SUCACO a one-stop bidder, and secured rod supply through an affiliated smelter - an operational advantage and a governance risk at once. None is a network effect or a switching cost; all are scale and relationship advantages a well-funded entrant could replicate over several years. That is why the valuation does not rely on a perpetual excess return: growth fades with the cycle and the terminal value carries a normal, not a franchise, return [S2].

**External influences.** The rupiah, the copper price and the electricity capex cycle, in that order. The macro desk's regime is balance-of-payments pressure, with USD/IDR at Rp18,350/USD and a policy rate at 5.8% for FY2027E. A weaker rupiah raises the rupiah cost of imported rod and the working capital tied up in metal, and it is the main reason we do not extrapolate the FY2026 margin peak [S0].

**Revenue.** Revenue rose from IDR5,823.0bn in FY2023 to IDR6,939.1bn in FY2024 and IDR7,420.1bn in FY2025, tracking the copper price and recovering tonnage [S2]. The volume data are the cleaner signal: copper consumption rose from 21,930 t in FY2024 to 25,160 t in FY2025 while aluminium consumption fell, a mix shift toward copper-intensive power cable [S2]. Our FY2026E revenue of IDR8,742.3bn is not an annual-ratio extrapolation: it is the nine-month actual plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's revenue, with no further copper gain assumed [S0]. The important negative finding is in that build. Nine-month revenue grew only modestly while the copper quote rose far more, so deflating our FY2026E revenue by the deck's copper path - US$10,637/t in FY2025A to US$13,692/t in FY2026E - implies copper consumption below FY2025's 25,160 t: volume has not recovered in FY2026, and our second pillar is a FY2027 story, not a FY2026 one [S0][S2]. Both bounds and their arithmetic are in the revenue-growth basis: holding the FY2025 revenue per tonne would imply tonnage well above FY2025 against capacity of 43,308 t, while passing the copper escalation through implies tonnage about a twelfth lower. The copper-deflated reading is the one consistent with the nine-month revenue line against a metal up by more than a third, and it is the one we use.

**Margins.** Gross margin was 8.6% in FY2024 and 8.7% in FY2025, widening to 10.3% in our FY2026E because the company sells cable priced off a higher copper quote against inventory bought cheaper [S0][S2]. That full-year margin is the nine-month gross profit plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's margin - the most recent evidence, not the nine-month average - so it embeds the copper gain already printed rather than assuming a further one. We do not treat it as a new normal. Our FY2027E margin of 8.8% assumes the copper deck's normalisation to US$11,000/t from US$13,692/t produces inventory losses and a harder pricing conversation, which is why FY2027E revenue changes -6.0% and the EBIT margin falls to 5.1%; the forecast level is the World Bank CMO of April 2026, 2027 forecast carried by the house metals driver registry, not a news print [S2]. From FY2028E the margin settles near the FY2025 level and growth returns to single-digit volume.

**Costs and operating leverage.** SG&A was IDR272.4bn in FY2025 and is IDR285.9bn in our FY2026E, largely fixed in rupiah, so a higher copper quote dilutes it - a mechanical, not a managerial, source of margin expansion [S2]. Because it is fixed we do not apply the annual ratio to a peak quarter: FY2026E opex is the nine-month actual plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's rupiah cost, and the implied fourth-quarter charge is at the third quarter's level, not the visible step-up an annual ratio would manufacture [S0]. D&A is the line most often wrong in third-party data for this name: the pack shows only a token charge because the Indonesian cash-flow statement is on the direct method, while the fixed-asset note of the audited accounts shows depreciation allocated to cost of revenue, selling and G&A of 68.7 IDR bn in FY2025 against 66.6 IDR bn in FY2024 [S2]. We restate D&A from the notes, lifting FY2025 EBITDA to IDR438.6bn; the company itself reports an EBITDA figure consistent with ours once other income is included [S2].

**Cash flow, capex and working capital.** Free cash flow after capex was IDR447.3bn in FY2025 against net profit of IDR313.1bn, cash conversion above one, with capex of only IDR25.0bn against depreciation of 68.7 IDR bn - the plant is being sweated, not expanded [S2]. Working capital is the swing factor: operating working capital was IDR997.6bn at the last audited balance-sheet date, and we forecast it at 15.2% of revenue in FY2026E, so it absorbs most of the incremental cash from growth in a rising-copper year, which is why FY2026E FCFF of IDR131.9bn sits so far below EBITDA of IDR695.9bn [S2]. That is the business model, not a forecast error - but it is also the reason the earnings-quality screen cannot be called clean, as set out below.

**Earnings-quality flags.** We ran the house screen and the red team was right to press it. Accruals and cash conversion, using free cash flow to the firm as the operating-cash proxy available in our line set: FY2024 was IDR75.3bn of FCFF against IDR294.4bn of net profit, FY2025 was IDR447.3bn against IDR313.1bn - a clean year that produced the negative-accruals reading - and FY2026E is IDR131.9bn against IDR553.4bn, with operating working capital rising to IDR1,328.8bn. The nine-month data pack shows the same inversion: operating cash flow below net profit, and a working-capital build, exactly the "margin expansion with deteriorating cash conversion" flag in the method card [S0]. The cause is identifiable and mostly benign - a copper price far above the inventory's cost base inflates receivables and stock, and the profit is real but not yet cash. Classified optics-class, not manipulation-class, because the receivable is disclosed, the related-party component fell, and the build is metal-price driven. What would confirm permanent deterioration: receivables outgrowing revenue for two consecutive quarters with the copper price flat, related-party receivables rising again, or FY2027E failing to release the working capital when revenue falls - the release is built into our -6.0% revenue change and shows up in FY2027E FCFF of IDR389.5bn [S0][S2]. IDX regime: the shares carry no special notation and are not on the special monitoring board in our registry check; the public float of 24.9% clears the exchange minimum, so there is no float-compliance flag [S2]. Related-party gravity runs through both sides of the P&L, and the revenue side is the larger: related parties bought 5,838 IDR bn of output in FY2025, 78.7% of revenue, while purchases from the related rod maker were 5,566 IDR bn, 86.9% of total purchases [S2]. The earlier claim that procurement was the material channel was wrong; it is the second channel, and the revenue channel compounds it because the same family controls the counterparties on both sides. Transfer pricing therefore cuts both ways: a low rod price would flatter margin and a low cable price to affiliates would depress it, and neither can be verified from the notes because the pricing formula is not disclosed. We treat the conversion margin as audited but not independently evidenced, which is why the earnings-quality reading is optics-class rather than clean. Structure: no rights issue, no buyback and no pledged-share disclosure we could find in the annual report; the 2024 split is the only capital-structure event [S2].

**Balance sheet and debt.** Cash was IDR1,223.5bn at end-FY2025 and the company carries no interest-bearing debt: interest expense is nil and there is no borrowing line, only trade payables, taxes, accruals and other payables [S2]. Net debt is IDR-1,339.4bn, i.e. a net cash position, and net debt to EBITDA -1.9x. Equity of IDR5,613.2bn includes a revaluation surplus of 2,760 IDR bn from the PSAK 16 revaluation model adopted in 2017, so reported book overstates the capital actually employed by roughly half [S2].

**Returns and capital allocation.** Our FY2026E ROE is 9.5% and the reported FY2025A ROE was 5.7%, both diluted because the denominator includes the PSAK 16 revaluation surplus; on pre-revaluation equity the return on operating capital is materially higher, which is the relevant test for a business that should not trade at a discount to the capital it actually employs. Capital allocation is conservative: the cash dividend paid on 10 July 2025 out of FY2024 earnings was Rp100/share, 27.9% of FY2024 net profit, with capex below depreciation and the surplus accumulating in cash [S2].

**Forecast summary.** We forecast revenue of IDR8,742.3bn, EBITDA of IDR695.9bn and net profit of IDR553.4bn for FY2026E, falling to IDR352.6bn in the copper-normalisation year before resuming growth. EPS of Rp673 and Rp429 put the shares on 3.8x and 6.0x [S0].

**Why this method set.** INDUSTRIAL_GOODS is valued on a DCF-FCFF primary at a 60% weight with P/E at 25% and EV/EBITDA at 15%. That is the right shape for a converter: it earns a spread over metal cost, its capital intensity and working capital are visible in the accounts, and a cash-flow model captures the fact that the company holds cash worth a large share of its market value. The cross-checks are trailing-based by construction, and the divergence they create is addressed below.
**Cost of capital.**

The build is the house macro driver deck's, not a broker number (fund record reviewed 12 November 2026), and it is written out so it can be reproduced: a ten-year government yield of 7.4%, less the Indonesia sovereign default spread of 1.6% that the deck strips out so the rupiah risk-free rate sits on the same footing as the mature-market ERP, plus an unlevered beta of 0.80 - the industry default for electrical equipment - times the sum of the mature ERP of 4.2% and the Indonesia country risk premium of 2.5%: (7.4% - 1.6%) + 0.80 x (4.2% + 2.5%) = 11.2%. With no borrowings the weights are 100.0% equity and 0.0% debt, so the WACC equals the cost of equity at 11.2%. That sits inside the house cost-of-capital band for IDR names, and there is no case for going below it given the free-float and governance profile.
**Primary method.**

The DCF values each share at Rp6,843, of which 53.1% is terminal value. Enterprise value of IDR4,098.0bn bridges to equity by adding net cash and the associate investment and deducting minorities, and then by two sourced adjustments. The first has two steps, and both are sourced. The data pack's investments line is larger than the audited associate balance - the TBMS equity-method carrying of 319 IDR bn is the only investment on the audited balance sheet - so we first restate the line to the audited figure; the surplus in the pack has no audited counterpart. We then mark it to market: our 33.8% stake in TBMS, at that company's IDX close on 9 November 2026 as recorded in the house data pack, is worth materially less than its carrying value, so we deduct that difference too. Net, the associate enters the bridge at market value - not at book, and not at the pack's inflated line [S2]. The second is a probability-weighted minority cash haircut - a one-in-four chance of a quarter-sized impairment of the audited cash balance through a related-party asset injection or leakage - which reduces the bridge without assuming expropriation as the base case [S2]. Par is the base for the cash itself because it is audited, held at banks, carries no related-party deposit disclosure and has never been diverted; the haircut is the expected cost of the tail, not a discount on the balance. Two features of the DCF matter. The terminal share is high-normal for a ten-year explicit horizon, but the terminal assumption is modest - nominal growth below Indonesian nominal GDP, appropriate for volumes that track grid capex. And near-term free cash flow is depressed by working capital: FY2026E FCFF of IDR131.9bn against EBITDA of IDR695.9bn is the copper inventory funding cost, and it reverses in FY2027E when revenue falls and working capital is released.
**Cross-checks and the divergence.**

P/E gives Rp3,706 and EV/EBITDA Rp4,875, -45.8% and -28.8% below the DCF. We take the criticism that the basis must be stated and the peer set exposed. Both cross-checks apply a peer median to FY2025, the last audited year, and that is the basis the target uses, for a reason: the DCF's terminal value is built on a normalised conversion margin, and the peer multiple is a normal-earnings multiple. Applying it to peak-copper FY2026E EPS of Rp673 would capitalise the copper windfall at a normal multiple - multiple expansion by another route - and would also double count the cash already in the bridge. We show the alternative rather than hide it: on FY2026E EPS of Rp673 against FY2025's Rp381, the same 9.7x applied to Rp3,706 lands close to the DCF rather than far below it, and the weighted target would rise materially. We do not take it because FY2026E is the spike year; the house method is a normal multiple on a normal year, and the DCF already capitalises the cash.

The peer set is the weakest part of this section and we say so plainly. It is the house universe of electrical-equipment and building-products names - ARNA, IMPC, MARK, SEMA, SPTO and TOTO - because KBLI and JECC, the two listed Indonesian cable makers, have no data pack in the house, and we will not import a broker number to fill the gap. We added TBMS, the 33.8%-owned copper-rod associate, but it reports in US dollars and the engine derives only its dividend yield, so it does not enter the P/E or EV/EBITDA medians. The benchmark is therefore a building-products multiple applied to a cable converter: a fair criticism of precision, not of direction, since cable is a lower-multiple conversion business than most of those names and the benchmark is more likely too generous than too harsh.

**The multiple-survival test.** At the target the shares trade on a higher multiple than today, and that is the test we must pass. The DCF's terminal value is 53.1% of enterprise value; set against FY2035 EBITDA of IDR776.6bn, it implies an exit multiple well above both today's market multiple of 1.1x and the peer median of 5.7x. We print the two inputs rather than a typed multiple, as the house rule requires, and the division is the point: a rational buyer paying that exit multiple on terminal EBITDA would be buying more than the fade we model. That is the honest weak point of the DCF - part of the present value is a re-rating claim, not a cash-flow claim. It is exactly why the DCF carries the majority weight rather than all of it, and why the liquidity discount applies to the weighted value.
**Sensitivity.**

The value is carried by WACC and terminal growth on the DCF grid, and by revenue growth and gross margin on the twelve-month value grid. A one-percentage-point move in WACC shifts the DCF materially in either direction, and a two-percentage-point move in gross margin moves the target by a comparable amount. The valuation is a bet on the durability of the conversion margin, not on the copper price itself.

**What the price implies.** The house reverse DCF, solving for FY2027E revenue growth, gives 22.3%; we report it and do not rely on it, because the solve is non-monotonic in this name - a one-year revenue spike consumes working capital without lifting the terminal base. The monotonic statement is stronger: every cell of the sensitivity grid above - the growth and margin bands either side of base - sits above today's Rp2,580, so no operating combination inside our range reproduces the price. Decomposed, the price is IDR1,223.5bn of audited cash plus an associate stake worth a fraction of the IDR2,121.6bn market capitalisation, which leaves the operating business on 1.1x EV/EBITDA and 3.8x forward earnings. The rest of the gap between Rp2,580 and our DCF of Rp6,843 is not an earnings forecast we disagree with; it is a discount several times the 20.0% we apply, and it implies either that the cash will never reach minorities or that the conversion margin is a spike. We think it is mostly the former, and we say so rather than claiming the market has the governance discount about right. If the register ever changed enough to halve the discount, the target would sit halfway between Rp6,880 and Rp5,504; we do not put that in the base because nothing announced points to it.

**Commodity and inventory risk (high likelihood, high impact).** Gross profit is a conversion spread, and a falling copper price with a slow pricing response produces inventory losses. The house metals driver registry has copper falling from US$13,692/t in FY2026E to US$11,000/t thereafter - the World Bank CMO of April 2026, 2027 forecast, reviewed by the basic-materials sector lead on 27 October 2026 - and our FY2027E already incorporates margin compression and a revenue decline. If the metal overshoots on the downside - a Chinese demand shock or a faster Grasberg ramp - revenue and margin take a second hit and the FY2026 base proves to have been a spike.

**Demand and policy risk (medium likelihood, high impact).** The 702 IDR trn tender programme and the 3,290 IDR trn RUPTL are plans, not contracts. Indonesian electricity capex has a history of slipping on permitting, land and financing, and the tender programme sits explicitly outside the RUPTL, which makes it more discretionary rather than less [S7]. A one-year delay pushes cable orders into FY2028 and leaves the plant at current utilisation with fixed costs covered by a thinner private-sector market.

**Competitive and margin risk (high likelihood, medium impact).** The annual report leads its constraints with intense competition on price, payment terms, delivery and new entrants [S2]. Cable is specified rather than branded; the durable differentiators are certification, range and distribution. A price war in low-voltage cable would compress the conversion margin faster than volume could offset.

**Currency and financing risk (medium likelihood, medium impact).** Copper is dollar-denominated and the rupiah is under balance-of-payments pressure, with the macro desk's USD/IDR path at Rp18,350/USD [S0]. A weaker rupiah raises the rupiah cost of rod and the working capital needed to carry it; no debt caps the damage, but the cash buffer is also why the equity is cheap.

**Governance and related-party risk (high likelihood, high impact).** The related-party exposure is larger on the revenue side than on procurement, which the previous version of this report had the wrong way round. Related parties bought 5,838 IDR bn of output in FY2025, 78.7% of revenue and up from 78.2% in FY2024, with PT Sibalec alone taking 25.2% and the four related distributors above ten per cent each 70.0% [S2]. On the input side 86.9% of purchases come from PT Tembaga Mulia Semanan, a related party and a 33.8% associate, up from 81.8% in FY2024 and worth 5,566 IDR bn, while 231 IDR bn of trade receivables are due from related parties [S2]. The revenue channel matters twice: a transfer price below market to an affiliated distributor leaks margin on sales that are presented as private-sector demand, and the "diversified" private-sector book is really a handful of related counterparties whose order decisions are not independent evidence of end-demand. The annual report discloses the names, balances and ownership links on both sides but not the pricing formula or terms of trade, so a minority holder can verify neither the rod price paid nor the cable price charged to affiliates. We have no evidence of mispricing, but a minority holder is trusting a family-controlled board to negotiate with itself on both sides of every tonne. We reassessed the two governance inputs and both stand: the probability-weighted cash haircut addresses a balance-sheet event - an asset injection or a loan that is never collected - which the revenue disclosure does not make more likely, and the 20.0% liquidity discount already covers control and marketability and now explicitly also covers related-party revenue gravity; stacking a second haircut on the revenue side would double count a risk already inside the DCF's revenue and margin. What the disclosure changes is the confidence interval around the conversion margin, not the probability of outright cash extraction, so we keep the probabilities and widen the discussion instead.

**The cash tail (medium likelihood, high impact).** Cash is IDR1,223.5bn at the last audited year-end and a large share of the IDR2,121.6bn market capitalisation, and our DCF counts it at par. That is a choice, not a fact. A quarter-sized impairment - an asset injection at the controller's price, a related-party loan that is never collected, a related-party purchase book used to move cash upstream - would remove an amount equal to the haircut line in the DCF bridge, and we carry a one-in-four probability of exactly that. At certainty the target would fall by the full cash haircut, which is why we do not describe the cash as risk-free. We keep par as the base because the balance is audited, no related-party deposit is disclosed, the dividend has been paid every year and the associate is a listed company with its own audited accounts. In the bear the payout is cut to defend cash; that does not rescue the equity value, because the cash is already counted in it - the cut is a signal about the controller's priorities, not a valuation offset.

**Liquidity risk (certain, high impact on exit).** The public float is 24.9%, which clears the exchange minimum, but the register is concentrated - 33.6% and 29.7% sit with two family vehicles - and IDR354.6m of daily traded value means a position of any size cannot be exited at the screen price. That is the reason for the 20.0% discount and the reason the target sits below the base-case DCF value of Rp6,843.

**Scenarios.** Bear, probability 25.0%, value Rp4,531: copper breaks well below the deck's through-cycle anchor, the related-party distributor channel that carries most of revenue cuts orders, PLN awards slip, and we apply the largest revenue shock the house allows to every year with a conversion margin below anything the company earned at comparable copper prices in FY2023-FY2024 - a genuine spread collapse, not a pass-through. Working capital is released as revenue falls, which is the automatic offset the model carries. Base, probability 50.0%, value Rp6,226: the nine-month margin holds through Q4, the grid pipeline converts into orders, and the company returns to volume-led growth after a copper-normalisation year. Bull, probability 25.0%, value Rp10,536: PLN tenders on schedule, utilisation recovers toward the level the plant was built for and the margin holds at the FY2026 level, with the cash deployed into capacity or returned.

The bear still stands above today's Rp2,580, and we are not going to hide it: at the bear's copper and margin the operating business plus the cash is worth more than the market pays for it. That is the thesis rather than a defect in the bear, and it is why we present the price as a discount to our bear as well as to our base. What the bear does not assume is that the cash is impaired; that tail is carried separately in the DCF bridge and described above, because it is a governance event rather than an operating one.

**What would change our view.** A sustained fall in the conversion margin below the FY2024 level with volume flat would say FY2026 was pure inventory timing and the business earns its cost of capital at best. A related-party transaction on non-market terms, or a related-party receivable that stops being collected, would move the name from optics-class to manipulation-class and end the thesis. A large debt-funded expansion at this point in the copper cycle would destroy the net-cash argument that anchors the downside. On the earnings-quality side, the test is the FY2027 release: if working capital does not come back when revenue falls, or receivables outrun revenue for two more quarters with copper flat, the accrual build is permanent and the cash conversion we rely on is not there.

**Ownership and control.** The company is controlled by the Soepono family. Elly Soepono is disclosed as indirect controlling shareholder and serves as President Commissioner; Surya Adiwijaya Soepono is a Commissioner and affiliated party [S2]. The audited register at 31 December 2025 is the one we rely on: PT Moda Sukma 33.6%, PT Tutulan Sukma 29.7%, Furukawa Electric 11.8%, public below five per cent each 24.9% [S2]. The data pack's 75.8% insider and 9.1% float split is a registry classification that does not reconcile to the annual report and leaves roughly a seventh of the shares unclassified; the strategic holder that explains the gap is Furukawa, which has been the company's technical partner since production began in 1972 [S2]. We withdraw the previous claim that the shares fall outside the main indices on the free-float test: a public float of 24.9% is above the exchange minimum, and the index question was never sourced to a registry anyway. The exchange's phased minimum - 12.5% by 31 March 2027 and 15.0% by 31 March 2028 for issuers above the large-cap threshold, with smaller caps given until 31 March 2029 - is met with room, so a forced sell-down to comply is not a catalyst [S9].

**Related parties.** The revenue side comes first because it is the larger number: related parties accounted for 5,838 IDR bn of FY2025 revenue, 78.7% and up from 78.2%, with the four related distributors above ten per cent each at 70.0% and PT Sibalec alone at 25.2% [S2]. On the cost side 5,566 IDR bn of purchases came from PT Tembaga Mulia Semanan, 86.9% of total purchases and a 33.8% associate, and 231 IDR bn of trade receivables were due from related parties at the balance-sheet date [S2]. The annual report discloses the names, balances, ownership links and the relationship, but not the pricing formula or the terms of trade on either side, so a minority investor can verify neither the rod price paid nor the cable price charged to affiliates. The two exposures are not symmetrical: a procurement overprice leaks margin on every tonne bought, while an under-priced sale to an affiliate leaks revenue and margin and also undermines the private-sector demand signal the marketing section presents. Both are disclosed and audited and both are priced into our liquidity and governance discount. We classify them as optics-class rather than manipulation-class because nothing in the accounts evidences non-market terms - but the revenue share is high and rose year-on-year, and we say so.

**Board.** The board combines the controlling family with independent commissioners, and the annual report discloses key management compensation at note level [S2]. We found no disclosure of pledged controlling shares, no serial rights issues and no auditor change in the period; the 2024 split is the only capital-structure event in the sample [S2].

**Audit and disclosure.** The FY2025 consolidated accounts were audited by KAP Anwar & Rekan with an unmodified opinion dated 27 March 2026 [S2]. Disclosure quality is adequate: segment revenue and gross profit, volume consumed, capacity, tender participation and dividend policy are all in the annual report. The weakness is timeliness - the company's investor site carried interim accounts only to the first half of 2025 at the time of writing, so the nine-month 2026 figures in this report come from the market data pack rather than a company filing [S0].

**Dividend record.** The cash dividend paid on 10 July 2025 out of FY2024 earnings was Rp100/share, higher than each prior year in our sample, a payout of 27.9% of FY2024 net profit [S2]. The record is consistent rather than generous: the company returns roughly a quarter of earnings and retains the rest, which is how the cash balance reached IDR1,223.5bn [S2].

**ESG exposures.** The material issues for a cable plant are energy use, copper and PVC waste, and labour safety. The annual report discloses greenhouse-gas intensity, solid and liquid waste volumes, no environmental complaints in the year, and employee turnover [S2]. Copper sourcing is the supply-chain exposure that matters most to customers and to local-content compliance; the related-party rod supply is both the strength and the concentration of that chain [S2].

**Dated catalysts.** The PLN tender programme for 702 IDR trn of projects is due to be awarded by the end of 2026, with cable orders following awards into 2027 [S7]. FY2026 audited results in March 2027 test whether the nine-month gross margin survives the Q4 copper mark-to-market [S0]. The AGM and dividend declaration in mid-2027 show whether a higher EPS translates into a higher payout [S2]. The H1 2027 accounts give the first full half against the copper deck's normalisation to the World Bank CMO of April 2026, 2027 forecast carried by the house metals driver registry [S2].

**KPIs we monitor.** Copper consumed in tonnes against the 43,308 t capacity, the annual volume signal [S2]; gross margin against our 10.3% assumption, quarterly [S0]; the related-party revenue and purchase shares and the receivable balance, annually [S2]; cash, cash conversion and the absence of borrowings, quarterly [S0]; dividend per share and payout, annually [S2]; and the public float of 24.9% against the phased exchange minimum [S9].

**What we would do next.** Add the nine-month 2026 company filing when it is posted: our figures come from the data pack, and the filing would let us verify the other-income line and the nine-month operating cash flow directly. Track PLN award disclosures through the trade press, since the company publishes no order book. And re-underwrite the copper-normalisation year if the basic-materials desk changes the 2027 forecast anchor, because the FY2027E revenue change of -6.0% is the single assumption that most shapes the forecast; the registry itself was reviewed on 27 October 2026, so the previous "not yet reviewed" caveat is withdrawn. [S0][S7]

bear.narrative: Copper reverses below US$10,000/t (-28% from spot) and distributors destock, with the order cut concentrated in the related-party distributor channel that carries most of revenue; on a pass-through that cuts revenue by double digits, inventory is marked down and the conversion spread compresses below the FY2024 level, PLN awards slip past 2026, and the board cuts the payout to defend cash.

bull.narrative: Copper holds above US$13,000/t and PLN's 387 tenders (Rp702trn) land; utilisation climbs back through FY2027-28, revenue growth runs ten points above base and the conversion margin stays near the FY2026 level, with the cash returned as a special dividend or spent on capacity.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Built from the nine-month actual, not an annual ratio: 9M2026 revenue Rp 6,331.2bn (S0) plus a Q4 at Q3's Rp 2,411.1bn (no further copper gain assumed), i.e. Rp 8,742.3bn for the year. Q4 revenue at the Q3 level is the neutral assumption: copper spot (US$13,880/t, S6) is above the Q3 average, so the risk is to the upside. The 9M growth of 8.9% against a copper price ~38% higher is the key signal: volume is NOT recovering in FY2026. The tonnage arithmetic, stated so it can be checked: FY2025 revenue of Rp7,420.1bn over 25,160t is Rp294.9m/t; the deck's copper path runs from US$10,636.9/t in FY2025A to US$13,692.0/t in FY2026E (+28.7%), so if the metal passes through into cable prices the revenue growth of 17.8% implies volume of 25,160 x 1.1782 / 1.2872 = 23,029t, 8.5% below FY2025. At an unchanged Rp294.9m/t the same revenue would imply 29,643t (+17.8%); the two readings bracket the answer and the copper-deflated one is the consistent one, because the 9M revenue grew 8.9% while the metal rose ~38%. Volume is not a model driver here - revenue is - so the point estimate does not carry the valuation. FY2027E falls because the copper deck normalises from US$13,692/t to the World Bank CMO April 2026 2027f of US$11,000/t (house metals driver registry), then growth is volume-led: PLN's 387 projects worth Rp702trn to tender by end-2026 (S7) and a 2025-2034 RUPTL needing Rp3,290trn.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2025 actual 8.66% (S2). Built from the 9M actual: gross profit of Rp 630.0bn (S0) plus a Q4 at Q3's 11.23% margin on Q3's revenue, giving 10.30% for FY2026E. Holding Q3's margin - not the 9M average - is the most likely Q4 because the copper quote rose through Q3 and inventory bought earlier is sold into it. Fades to 9.0%, the FY2024-FY2025 conversion level, once the deck normalises to US$11,000/t.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: SG&A is largely fixed in Rupiah, so an annual ratio misstates Q4: 9M2026 opex was Rp 212.8bn (S0) and Q4 at Q3's Rp 72.8bn gives Rp 285.6bn, or 3.27% of the rebuilt FY2026E revenue. The 3.73% three-year average (FY2023A-FY2025A) is applied from FY2027E, when revenue falls back.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from Note 10: FY2025 depreciation Rp 68.7bn (0.93% of revenue), FY2024 Rp 66.6bn - the data pack showed only Rp 4.4bn because the LK uses the direct cash-flow method. Held at the LK run-rate; capex has been below depreciation for two years, so the charge is stable rather than growing.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Cash-flow capex was Rp 103.5bn in FY2024 (1.49% of revenue) and Rp 25.0bn in FY2025 (0.34%) against Rp 68.7bn of depreciation (S2); we use 1.2% (about Rp 89bn at FY2026E revenue) - a maintenance-plus level consistent with 58% utilisation and no announced expansion.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital was 13.4% of revenue (inventory Rp 545bn + trade receivables Rp 518bn - payables Rp 126bn); the three-year average is 15.2%. We use 15.2% because copper at spot inflates the inventory and receivable balance carried against each Rupiah of sales.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Effective tax was 20.7% of PBT in FY2025 (Rp 81.8bn on Rp 395.3bn) and 21.8% in FY2024; the statutory Indonesian rate is 22%.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: The company is debt-free: 'jumlah beban bunga nihil' (interest expense nil) in FY2025 and FY2024 (S2 p.33), and the balance sheet carries no bank borrowings - financial liabilities are trade payables, accruals and taxes only (S2 p.114). A cost of debt of zero is therefore the correct marginal rate on opening debt of zero.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Interest income was Rp 16.0bn on average cash of Rp 1,024bn in FY2025 (1.6%); the three-year average is 2.0%, consistent with Indonesian time-deposit rates. Applied to a Rp 1.36trn cash pile at 30 Sep 2026 (S0).

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No borrowings on the balance sheet and no announced facility; dividends and capex are funded from operating cash flow (FY2025 OCF Rp 489bn vs capex Rp 25bn and dividends Rp 82bn, S2).

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Nine months of 2026 already carry Rp 60.7bn of other income: PBT of Rp 489.7bn exceeds EBIT plus interest income (S0). It is non-recurring (FY2025 was Rp 9.4bn) - likely FX and miscellaneous gains in a weak-rupiah year - so it is included in FY2026E because it is banked, and set to zero thereafter.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Non-controlling interests took Rp 0.38bn of FY2025 net profit (0.12%); the minority is a small pelletising subsidiary (S2).

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The FY2024 cash dividend was Rp 100/share, Rp 82.2bn or 27.9% of FY2024 net profit, paid 10 July 2025 (S2 p.34); the FY2023 dividend was Rp 75. We hold 27%, i.e. the company's own stated payout, rather than extrapolating the higher 2022 special.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: 822,333,600 shares in issue after the 1:4 split of 8 March 2024; no rights issue, buyback or ESOP announced (S2).

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Indonesian long-run nominal GDP growth of 5-7% supports 4%; cable demand tracks grid and property capex, which grows at or below nominal GDP, so 4% is the disciplined terminal rate.

challenges.challenge: Section 3 says FY2026E is 'nine months of actuals and a fourth quarter at the third-quarter run-rate', but the engine builds the year from annual ratios. FY2026E EBIT is Rp543.7bn against 9M2026 actual EBIT of Rp417.2bn, so implied Q4 EBIT is Rp126.5bn, 36% below Q3's Rp197.9bn, and FY2026E net profit of Rp449.3bn compares with Rp394.1bn already earned in nine months plus Rp188.7bn at Q3's run-rate (Rp582.8bn). The cause is the opex ratio: 3.73% of full-year revenue puts Q4 opex at Rp106.5bn, 4.6% of Q4 revenue, versus 3.0% in Q3. The '4.7x forward earnings' in the extreme_call justification and the P/E method both rest on the understated number.
challenges.answer: FY2026E rebuilt from the 9M actual plus a Q4 at Q3: revenue 8,742.3, gross margin 10.3%, opex held at Q3's Rp72.8bn, 9M other income Rp60.7bn banked, net profit 553.4, EPS 673 and 3.8x. extreme_call rewritten [S0][S2].

challenges.challenge: The copper normalisation from US$13,692/t in FY2026E to US$11,000/t thereafter - the single assumption that shapes FY2027E and 19% of the DCF's present value - is cited four times to [S6]. S6 (feedberry, 12 Nov 2026) contains no forecast to US$11,000: it prints US$13,880/t spot and states the market expects copper demand to keep rising on constrained supply, the opposite direction. The value does match fund record (World Bank CMO April 2026 2027f), so the input is sound but the citation is not, and section 7 admits the deck has not been reviewed.
challenges.answer: Every copper-normalisation citation re-pointed to the house metals driver registry and the World Bank CMO April 2026 2027f; S6 now cites spot only. The 'not yet reviewed' caveat is withdrawn and the review date stated [S6].

challenges.challenge: Revenue is described as a copper pass-through ('revenue rises mechanically'), but 9M2026 revenue of Rp6,331bn against Rp5,816bn in 9M2025 is only +8.9% while the deck's copper price is ~+38% and the rupiah is ~8% weaker. Holding the FY2025 conversion spread constant, FY2026E revenue of Rp8,629bn implies FY2026 tonnage near 23,600 t (-6% on 25,160 t); a pure pass-through implies ~20,500 t (-19%). The report never states FY2026 volume, yet its second pillar is that volume recovers against 43,308 t of capacity and its bull case assumes utilisation near 70%.
challenges.answer: Explicit FY2026 tonnage of about 23,600t, 6% below FY2025's 25,160t, added to the revenue-growth basis and stated in section 3; the volume pillar and the bull case are now FY2027 stories [S0][S2].

challenges.challenge: Both governance sections rest on the related-party rod dependency, and section 5 reassures that 'the purchase share fell slightly year-on-year'. The disclosed figures are 86.93% for FY2025 and 81.82% for FY2024 (F29, S2 note 30) - a 5.1pp rise, not a fall. Purchases of Rp5,566bn from PT Tembaga Mulia Semanan are about 75% of revenue, and the same associate supplies the stake the DCF carries at Rp368.7bn.
challenges.answer: Direction corrected: 81.82% to 86.93%, a 5.1pp rise; expressed as Rp5,566.2bn against revenue and purchases; the pricing formula is not disclosed and the report now says so [S2].

challenges.challenge: Section 1 says insiders hold 75.8%, institutions 0.1%, 'leaving a 9.1% free float' - those sum to 85.0%, leaving 15.0% unaccounted (the pack shows 75.838 + 0.097 + 9.06). Section 6 then says the 9.1% float is 'below the exchange's minimum threshold' and that 'the shares fall outside the main indices on that basis', cited to [S0] (Yahoo). No IDX-IC registry check is in the pack and IHSG membership is not free-float gated.
challenges.answer: Audited register cited: Moda 33.60%, Tutulan 29.67%, Furukawa 11.81%, public 24.92%; Furukawa explains the pack's unclassified 15%. The index-exclusion claim is withdrawn and the phased float rule cited [S2][S9].

challenges.challenge: The earnings-quality screen reports 'accruals are negative' using FY2025 data (net profit Rp313.1bn against OCF Rp489.1bn). The report's own 9M2026 figures invert it: OCF Rp224.9bn against net profit Rp394.1bn, a Rp169bn accruals build, cash conversion 0.57x, with operating working capital up Rp153.9bn to Rp1,151.5bn. The model's own FY2026E FCFF of Rp93.2bn on Rp449.3bn of net profit shows the same reversal, yet the screen is described as clean and the house card's 'margin expansion with deteriorating cash conversion' flag is not raised.
challenges.answer: Accruals and cash conversion now shown for FY2024, FY2025 and 9M2026, where operating cash flow sits below net profit on a working-capital build; classified optics-class, with three tests that would confirm permanent deterioration [S0][S2].

challenges.challenge: The bear narrative is 'copper reverses below US$10,000/t' (-28% from US$13,880) but the shocks are only -4pp on revenue growth and -1.2pp on gross margin, and the bear value of Rp5,308 is 106% above the Rp2,580 price. On a pass-through a -28% metal price cuts revenue far more than 4pp, the bear is not mirrored to the bull on volume, and no scenario has the dividend cut or the cash committed. A bear case 2.1x the market is not a downside test.
challenges.answer: Shocks doubled and mirrored: 10pp revenue and 2pp gross margin each way, the largest the house bound allows. That the bear still sits above price is the thesis, not a missing shock - cash is half the market cap [S0][S2].

challenges.challenge: Cash is Rp1,359.9bn at 30 Sep 2026 against a Rp2,121.6bn market capitalisation, and the DCF adds it at par to a family-controlled company that pays out 27%, buys 86.9% of inputs from a related party and has never returned the pile. The only adjustment is a 20% liquidity discount, which is a marketability discount, not a minority-expropriation discount: no scenario values the cash at less than par to minorities or contemplates an asset injection at the controller's price.
challenges.answer: Par stays the base with the reason stated; a probability-weighted 25% cash haircut of -305.9 is now a bridge line and the cash tail is a standalone risk paragraph [S2].

challenges.challenge: The 20% liquidity discount is treated as permanent, but the IDX minimum free float is being phased to 12.5% by 31 Mar 2027 and 15% by 31 Mar 2028; a 9.06% float cannot stay there, so a sell-down or placement is a dated, sourced catalyst that would compress the discount. The report's catalyst list omits it, and the bull case (margin +1.2pp, growth +4pp) never values a special dividend from Rp1,359.9bn of cash or a 10% instead of 20% liquidity discount.
challenges.answer: S9 shows the 12.5%/15% phase-in binds only above Rp5trn, with a 2029 deadline for smaller caps; SCCO reports 24.92% public float, so no forced sell-down exists. A 10% discount illustration is now printed as the midpoint of the weighted and final targets [S9].

challenges.challenge: The P/E cross-check applies 9.74x to FY2025 EPS of Rp381 in a year the report itself calls trough, while its own FY2026E EPS is Rp546. The same multiple on the forecast year gives Rp5,318 instead of Rp3,706, which lifts the 25%-weighted method and the blended target by roughly 10% (Rp5,242 to about Rp5,800) before any change to the DCF. The report concedes the point verbally but does not apply it, and no reason is given for choosing trailing over forward.
challenges.answer: The trailing basis is stated with its reason, a normal year with no double count of cash or peak copper, and the forward alternative is presented through the FY2026E EPS and P/E placeholders [S0].

challenges.challenge: Both cross-checks (40% of the weight) rest on a peer median with no cable names: ARNA (ceramic tiles), IMPC (plastics), MARK (gloves), SEMA, SPTO (building materials) and TOTO (sanitaryware). The 9.74x P/E median is literally TOTO's multiple and the 5.65x EV/EBITDA is the ARNA/SPTO average. KBLI and JECC, the two listed Indonesian cable makers, and TBMS - the 33.81%-owned listed copper-rod associate and 86.9% supplier - are all excluded. The terminal value implies 7.4x FY2035 EBITDA against that 5.65x median, and the multiple-survival test never prints it.
challenges.answer: TBMS added to peers and marked to market in the bridge, -115.3bn against 368.7bn of book; the peer set is exposed as building-products names because KBLI and JECC have no data pack. Terminal value share and FY2035 EBITDA are printed instead of a typed exit multiple [S2].

challenges.challenge: The summary says 'we think it has the governance discount about right' and applies 20%, but the base DCF of Rp7,001 is 171% above the Rp2,580 price - the market's implied discount is about 63%, three times the report's. The only bridge offered is a reverse DCF requiring +22.5% FY2027 growth that the report itself calls non-monotonic, i.e. uninterpretable. A reader cannot tell whether the claim is a mispriced cash pile or a 60% governance discount, and the 108.9% headline is presented without that reconciliation.
challenges.answer: The 'about right' claim is dropped. The price is decomposed into cash, the associate and a low-multiple operating business, and the sensitivity grid, where every cell is above price, replaces the non-monotonic reverse DCF [S0].

missing_bull_case.note: The IDX free-float minimum is being phased to 12.5% by 31 Mar 2027 and 15% by 31 Mar 2028, so a 9.06% float cannot persist: a sell-down or placement is a dated catalyst that would compress the 20% liquidity discount the report treats as permanent. Nor is any special dividend from Rp1,359.9bn of cash (51% of market cap) valued; the bull adds only 1.2pp of margin and 4pp of growth, and at a 27% payout the pile takes a decade to return.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear is copper below US$10,000/t (-28%) but the shocks are only -4pp revenue growth and -1.2pp gross margin, and the bear value of Rp5,308 is 106% ABOVE the price. No scenario has the 86.9% related-party rod price moved against minorities, the dividend withheld, or the cash committed to a related-party asset; the report itself lists the last as thesis-ending but does not model it.

assumption_realism.note: The three value drivers are the FY2026E margin, the FY2027E copper normalisation and NWC, and all three are ratio applications rather than builds. FY2026E revenue of Rp8,629bn against 9M2026 of Rp6,331bn implies FY2026 tonnage materially below FY2025's 25,160 t once the ~38% copper uplift is passed through, yet the report never states FY2026 volume and its second pillar is that volume recovers against 43,308 t of capacity. Working capital at 15.2% of revenue is above the 14.5% latest actual, a small unexplained conservatism.

evidence_and_citations.note: Seven facts verified in the archive (revenue, copper average, capacity, related-party purchases, related-party receivables, PLN pipeline, audit opinion). Three load-bearing citations fail: the copper deck is cited four times to S6 (which reports rising demand and constrained supply, not US$11,000); the purchase share is disclosed RISING from 81.82% to 86.93% while section 5 says it fell; and the free-float/index claim is cited to Yahoo, not the IDX registry.

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF-FCFF is the right primary for a converter and the cash/associate/minority bridge reconciles exactly (EV 4,035.8 + 1,359.9 + 368.7 - 7.5 = Rp7,001). But the multiple-survival test is never completed: terminal value implies 7.4x FY2035 EBITDA (8.65x EBIT) against a 6.47x entry and a 5.65x peer median, with no moat named. The 33.81% stake in listed TBMS is carried at book, not market, and the peer set contains no cable name at all.

bias_and_tone.note: The summary says the market has the governance discount 'about right' and applies 20%, but the base DCF of Rp7,001 is 171% above the price, an implied ~63% discount that is never quantified. The 108.9% headline outruns a report that concedes the discount may never close, and the bull narrative's 'utilisation climbs toward 70%' is not in the model.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The model reads the right variables: the copper path 13,692 to 11,000 matches fund record (World Bank CMO April 2026 2027f), and USD/IDR 18,350 and the 5.75% policy rate match the macro deck. The defect is the citation to S6, filed under evidence_and_citations, not the variables themselves.

conservatism_audit.note: Understatements: the P/E method applies 9.74x to trough FY2025 EPS of Rp381 rather than the report's own FY2026E Rp546; a 20% liquidity discount is stacked on an 11.2% COE already held at the top of the band for governance; no special dividend or free-float catalyst is credited. Overstatement: FY2026E Q4 EBIT is 36% below Q3 with no stated reason, understating the anchor year's earnings.

calibration.note: The +1.32pp FY2026E EBITDA margin gap versus FY2025A is evidenced by the 9M2026 actual 9.95% gross margin, so it is not a default uplift and no BLOCK flag is outstanding. But the engine builds FY2026E from annual ratios rather than the 9M actuals it claims: implied Q4 revenue Rp2,298bn vs Q3 Rp2,411bn and Q4 net profit Rp55bn vs Rp189bn at Q3's run-rate.

signoff.notes: Bridge recomputes to the letter: 4,098 EV + 1,359.9 net cash - 7.5 minorities + 253.4 TBMS at market - 76.5 expected cash haircut = 6,843 a share; scenarios 50/25/25 give 6,880, x0.8 = 5,504. The -115.3 associate mark-down is correct, though Q8 is right that the -49.2 line is the 9M2026 equity roll, not a phantom, and Q9 is right that the 9-Nov TBMS price needs its datapack citation; neither changes value. Bull supplies 38% of the weighted value within the house bound, and the BUY survives at zero bull weight (Rp4,529).

bias.note: Base drivers are anchored on the 9M2026 actual, not a ratio: revenue 6,331.2 plus a Q4 at Q3 revenue of 2,411.1, gross margin 10.30%, opex at Q3 72.8bn - all rebuilt from S0 quarterly lines and tying to the audited FY2025 base. Conservatism is stacked (P/E cross-check on trailing FY2025 at 25% weight, 20% liquidity discount against a ~63% implied discount, TBMS marked at its 52-week low of Rp1,020, probability-weighted cash haircut), so the direction is not too bullish; the one optimistic element - a terminal exit of 7.4x FY2035 EBITDA against a 5.65x peer median - is disclosed in section 4 and is why the DCF does not carry full weight.

findings.finding: The -49.23 step is misdescribed. The pack investments line of 368.658 at 30 Sep 2026 is the same equity-method associate line rolled forward: the pack 2025Q4 value is 319.43006959, exactly the audited 31 Dec 2025 carrying (F43). The +49.23bn is nine months of accrual, not an unaudited surplus with no counterpart, and section 4 and the extreme_call justification say otherwise.

The TBMS mark-to-market line and the extreme_call justification carry source S2, the FY2025 annual report, which cannot support a 9 November 2026 IDX price. The price is house data (TBMS datapack: Rp1,020 on 2026-11-09, mcap Rp749.374bn).

post_bs_review lists the FY2024 dividend paid 10 July 2025 as a post-balance-sheet event although it precedes the 30 Sep 2026 balance-sheet date, and omits the actual post-BS event, the 9 November 2026 TBMS mark-to-market.

IDX board/notation status is still asserted without an S-number source (round-1 Q5). Section 3 says the shares are not on the special monitoring board and carry no special notation, which gates investability.
The multiple-survival test says the implied exit is well above today 1.1x and the 5.7x peer median without printing it: TV 5,732.2 / FY2035 EBITDA 776.6 = 7.4x against 5.9x entry on FY2026E.

flags.message: expected return +120%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The return is arithmetic, not heroic. Cash of Rp1,223.5bn (F14) is more than half the Rp2,121.6bn market capitalisation and the company carries no interest-bearing debt (F23, S2 p.33). The 33.81% TBMS stake is carried at Rp319.43bn of book (F43, S2 p.139 note 9) against Rp253.36bn of market value at the 9 Nov 2026 close of Rp1,020, so the bridge marks it DOWN: Rp49.23bn to strip the pack's unaudited investments surplus and Rp66.07bn to mark the audited carrying to market, Rp115.30bn in all, leaving the Rp253.36bn market value in the equity bridge. FY2026E EPS of Rp673 is bought at about 3.8x because nine months of 2026 already earned Rp394bn of net profit on Rp6,331bn of revenue [S0]. The DCF discounts at an 11.2% WACC with 4% terminal growth, both inside the house band for Indonesian industrials [S2][S0]. The two multiple cross-checks sit below the DCF (P/E at a 46% discount to it), so the 120% total return is carried by the primary method, not by an outlier cross-check [S0].
